subject: Request: temporary feature bypass for ThunderBridge exec go/no-go
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary feature bypass for ThunderBridge exec go/no-go

Hi team,

Quick background: ThunderBridge (contact Priya; cc'd below in later messages) is at the final exec review for a multi-region Dedicated commitment. Their blocker is a very specific routing/affinity requirement: they need a tenant-level model affinity pin when their traffic spikes so we can guarantee sub-50ms tail latency for a class of low-latency endpoints.

We have a narrow window — they want a firm answer before their exec meeting on Wednesday 6/2. Can Product/Eng evaluate a time-limited, guarded bypass that:
- allows a tenant to opt into a temporary "model-affinity override" (pin to a smaller footprint variant)
- automatically reverts after 72 hours unless extended by Ops
- exposes telemetry for impact (latency, token throughput, CPU/GPU utilization)

I've attached a short mutual action plan that explains the business ask and timeline (TB_MutualActionPlan_v2.pdf). From Sales perspective this is high-propensity — if we can commit something low-risk for a short window we close the deal.

Asks:
- Karthik: feasibility + product constraints and a proposed acceptance criteria
- Jonas: quick engineering sketch, security/observability guardrails, rough effort estimate
- Marissa: any CS/ops gotchas we need in the SOW/SLA to limit blast radius

If we can land an approach that is safe, declarative, and reversible, we can offer it as a one-time activation (flag + audit trail) and move forward.

Thanks — appreciate quick turnaround.

—Grace
Grace O'Connor
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary feature bypass for ThunderBridge exec go/no-go

Grace — thanks for the context and the MAP. I skimmed the attachment, and a few immediate notes:

1) Product constraints: we don't currently have a concept of a temporary tenant-level "pin" that both preserves tail-latency while remaining fully reversible without operator intervention. Adding a controlled override is possible but requires guardrails around routing, capacity accounting, and an automatic rollback.

2) Acceptance criteria I propose:
- feature toggle that only accepts pre-authorized tenant IDs
- automatic telemetry tag for every request while the override is active
- an audit log entry + irreversible DocuSign-backed change in the SOW or a signed one-off addendum (legal has asked for auditable consent)

3) Alternatives: a config-level priority lane (no code change to runtime) that Ops schedules for a tenant. This is quicker but less deterministic for latency.

Before I commit, two clarifying questions:
- Is the target window strictly 72 hours?
- Do they require zero-variation in model outputs (i.e., pin to same exact model weights) or is a compatible variant acceptable?

If the answers are: yes to the 72 hours and compatible-variant is okay, I think we can deliver a product-approved fast-path in ~2 sprints with Jonas' help to scope the runtime changes. If they insist on identical weights and strict determinism, that looks like more work and a more invasive change.

Karthik
Product Lead — Serving Platform

Thanks for pulling this together. Technical take:

Short answer: feasible as a scoped, short-lived capability if we treat it as a runtime "operational shim" rather than a model-level change. High-level approach:
- Implement a tenant override flag in the routing layer that forces affinity to a pre-warmed pool of compatible model variants (not the canonical production weights unless requested)
- The override is timeboxed (TTL enforced by control plane) and requires a signed activation token to prevent accidental enabling
- Telemetry: inject a "tb_override" tag in spans + per-tenant metrics dashboard; Ops command to revoke immediately

Risk/notes:
- This will increase cold-start and capacity reservation pressure; we should limit concurrent active overrides per-region
- Quantization/variant drift could cause small output differences — call this out in the SOW

Effort: rough T-shirting — 2 engineers x 3 sprints to implement control-plane flag, safe rollout, and dashboards (includes tests + a short canary). If we go the config-only path Karthik suggested, we can do it in 1 sprint but with less latency determinism.

I attached a quick diagram (design-sketch.png) showing the routing shim and telemetry hooks. Happy to sync for 30 minutes tomorrow to align on acceptance criteria.

—Jonas
Principal Engineer, Runtime

We had a pre-brief with our CFO and CTO. Both teams want the temporary override path rather than a long-term engineering commitment if it can be delivered with the safety guarantees you outline. They specifically asked that the activation be reversible by Redwood within a 15-minute window and that the SOW explicitly call out any functional drift if non-identical variants are used.

We're prepared to sign the one-off addendum and SOW if you can provide:
- a short technical description we can show to our CTO (one-pager)
- DocuSign-ready SOW (SOW_ThunderBridge_v3.pdf placeholder)

We've attached our internal risk checklist separately (not included here) and have a hard exec review on 2027-06-02 09:00 PT.

Best,
Priya Menon
